evidence: This is a result from the screen data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Top gene hits identified through both screens involved in TNFα signaling include CFLAR, MAPK1, RIPK1, TNFRSF1A, and ICAM1.
source: Top gene hits identified through both screens involved in for example TNFα signaling were CFLAR, MAPK1, RIPK1, TNFRSF1A, and ICAM1, highlighting their role in regulating tumor sensitivity to TNF-α-induced cell death.
evidence: This is a result from the screen data with an interpretation.

claim: The identification of genes involved in IFN-γ signaling (PTPN2, SOCS1, STAT1, JAK2) were consistent with previous findings and validated the complementary CRISPR screen approach.
source: The identification of genes involved in IFN-γ signaling (PTPN2, SOCS1, STAT1, JAK2) were consistent with previous findings and validated our complementary CRISPR screen approach (Lawson et al., 2020; Patel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the screen data compared to previous literature.

claim: The screen data showed overlaps with previously performed screens in genes regulating autophagy (PIK3C3, ATG3, ATG10, ATG13).
source: Furthermore, our data showed additional overlaps with previously performed screens in genes regulating for example autophagy (PIK3C3, ATG3, ATG10, ATG13) thus controlling susceptibility to CTL attack (Lawson et al., 2020; Young et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a result from the screen data compared to previous literature.

claim: Enrichment of genes regulating antigen processing and presentation were not found among the top hits in the complementary CRISPR screen presumably due to direct loading of the antigenic peptide on tumor cells.
source: In contrast to other studies, enrichment of genes regulating antigen processing and presentation were not found among the top hits in our complementary CRISPR screen presumably due to direct loading of the antigenic peptide on tumor cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the screen data with an interpretation of the reason.

claim: Addition of TAK1 inhibitor (Takinib) significantly enhanced tumor killing in a dose-dependent manner compared to control condition.
source: Addition of Takinib significantly enhanced tumor killing in a dose-dependent manner compared to control condition rendering tumor cells more sensitive to TNFα-induced cell death (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: TAK1 inhibitor renders tumor cells more sensitive to TNFα-induced cell death.
source: Addition of Takinib significantly enhanced tumor killing in a dose-dependent manner compared to control condition rendering tumor cells more sensitive to TNFα-induced cell death (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The role of ICAM-1 in the immune response is well documented.
source: The role of ICAM-1 in the immune response is well documented but its role in regulating anti-tumor response and tumor-CTL interaction remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the literature.

claim: The role of ICAM-1 in regulating anti-tumor response and tumor-CTL interaction remains elusive.
source: The role of ICAM-1 in the immune response is well documented but its role in regulating anti-tumor response and tumor-CTL interaction remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about gaps in current knowledge.

claim: Other ICAM family members were not identified in the screen.
source: Although there are other ICAM family members with overlapping functions and the ability to bind similar ligands (Binnerts et al., 1994; Campanero et al., 1993; Casasnovas et al., 1999), we did not identify other ICAMs in our screen.
evidence: This is an observation from the screen data.

claim: The most important ICAM-1 ligand for the interaction between CTLs and tumor cells is LFA-1.
source: The most important ICAM-1 ligand for the interaction between CTLs and tumor cells is LFA-1 (Jenkinson et al., 2005; Marlin and Springer, 1987).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LFA-1 is present on the antigen-specific CTLs used in this model.
source: LFA-1 is present on the antigen-specific CTLs used in this model (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ICAM-1 deletion led to resistance to CTL killing in all cell lines tested (HCT 116, Panc-1 and UACC-257).
source: ICAM-1 deletion led to resistance to CTL killing in all cell lines tested (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Resistance to CTL killing induced by ICAM-1 deletion could not be attributed to an increase in antigen presentation as HLA-A2 cell surface level was not affected by ICAM1 depletion.
source: Resistance could not be attributed to an increase in antigen presentation as HLA-A2 cell surface level was not affected by ICAM1 depletion (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: PD-L1 level on the cell surface was increased in UACC-257 cells upon ICAM1 depletion induced by sgRNA2.
source: PD-L1 level on the cell surface was increased in UACC-257 cells upon ICAM1 depletion induced by sgRNA2 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5D (note: the text references Figure 5D but this appears to be an error as the figure shows Figure 4D).

claim: The interaction of PD-1 on antigen-specific CTLs with PD-L1 had little to no role in the interaction of activated CTLs with tumor cells in this system.
source: Our results demonstrate that the interaction of PD-1 on antigen-specific CTLs (Figure 4G) with PD-L1 had little to no role in the interaction of activated CTLs with tumor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4E, F, G.

claim: PD-1/PD-L1 blockade may rather increase T cell priming and expansion.
source: PD-1/PD-L1 blockade may rather increase T cell priming and expansion (Borst et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2018; Peng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In this system, ICAM-1 plays a crucial role in the productive interaction between tumor and activated CTL.
source: Altogether these results show that in our system, ICAM-1 plays a crucial role in the productive interaction between tumor and activated CTL and that ICAM-1 depletion has more effect than PD-1 overexpression in inducing killing resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ICAM-1 depletion has more effect than PD-1 overexpression in inducing killing resistance.
source: Altogether these results show that in our system, ICAM-1 plays a crucial role in the productive interaction between tumor and activated CTL and that ICAM-1 depletion has more effect than PD-1 overexpression in inducing killing resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Multiple isoforms of ICAM-1 exist including secreted variants.
source: Multiple isoforms of ICAM-1 exist including secreted variants (Ramos et al., 2014; Seth et al., 1991; Wakatsuki et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Secreted ICAM-1 may function as LFA-1 antagonist.
source: Secreted ICAM-1 may in fact function as LFA-1 antagonist (Meyer et al., 1995) altogether mimicking ICAM-1 deficiency by disrupting mICAM-1/LFA1 interaction.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Shedding of ICAM-1 from the cell surface is mediated by several proteases including MMP-9.
source: Shedding of ICAM-1 from the cell surface is mediated by several proteases including MMP-9 (Fiore et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The substitution of proline in position 404 with glutamic acid (P404E) inhibited shedding of ICAM-1 in the presence of MMP-9 without affecting mICAM-1 levels.
source: The substitution of proline in position 404 with glutamic acid (P404E) inhibited shedding of ICAM-1 in the presence of MMP-9 without affecting mICAM-1 levels (Fiore et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ICAM-1 cleavage process is regulated by multiple kinases acting through specific tyrosine residues Y474 and Y485 within the cytoplasmic region of ICAM-1.
source: ICAM-1 cleavage process is regulated by multiple kinases acting through specific tyrosine residues Y474 and Y485 within the cytoplasmic region of ICAM-1 (Tsakadze et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The fraction of eGFP+ cells after transfection was similar between all ICAM-1 variants reflecting equal transfection efficiency.
source: The fraction of eGFP + cells after transfection was similar between all ICAM-1 variants reflecting equal transfection efficiency (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Mutant versions of ICAM-1, Y474A+Y485A and P404E, were previously described to inhibit proteolytic cleavage and subsequent shedding of ICAM-1 in other cell types.
source: Mutant versions of ICAM-1, Y474A+Y485 A and P404E, were previously described to inhibit proteolytic cleavage and subsequent shedding of ICAM-1 in other cell types (Fiore et al., 2002; Tsakadze et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In HCT 116 cells, neither mICAM-1 levels nor secreted amounts of sICAM-1 were altered after transfection with Y474A+Y485A or P404E mutants compared to full length ICAM-1.
source: In our model, neither mICAM-1 levels (Figure 5D) nor secreted amounts of sICAM-1 (Figure 5E) were altered after transfection compared to full length ICAM-1.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: The Y474A+Y485A and P404E mutations are not relevant for ICAM-1 cleavage under these conditions in HCT 116 cells.
source: These results indicate that these mutations are not relevant for ICAM-1 cleavage under these conditions in HCT 116 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Transfection of sICAM1 in ICAM1 KO cells resulted in no detectable flag-tag expression on the cell surface, but enhanced sICAM-1 levels in the supernatant 5.21±0.42 fold.
source: Transfection of sICAM1 in ICAM1 KO cells resulted in no detectable flag-tag expression on the cell surface, but enhanced sICAM-1 levels in the supernatant 5.21±0.42 fold (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Reintroduction of full length ICAM1 in ICAM1 KO resulted in 2.21±0.11 fold higher sICAM-1 levels.
source: Additionally, reintroduction of full length ICAM1 in ICAM1 KO resulted in 2.21±0.11 fold higher sICAM-1 levels.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data.

claim: ICAM1 KO cells secrete 4-fold less sICAM-1 compared to WT cells.
source: Inversely, ICAM1 KO cells secrete 4-fold less compared to WT cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Levels of sICAM-1 in the supernatants of WT cells transfected with sICAM1 were 2.39±0.19 fold higher than in control WT cells.
source: Levels of sICAM-1 in the supernatants of WT cells transfected with sICAM1 were 2.39±0.19 fold higher than in control WT cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The expression of full-length ICAM1 rescued antigen-specific tumor cell killing by CTLs in ICAM1 KO cells.
source: The expression of full-length ICAM1 rescued antigen-specific tumor cell killing by CTLs in ICAM1 KO cells confirming the important role of ICAM-1 in controlling CTL-mediated killing (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The mutant ICAM1 P404E rescued tumor killing by CTLs to similar extent as full length ICAM1.
source: The mutant ICAM1 P404E rescued tumor killing by CTLs to similar extent as full length ICAM1, whereas no rescue could be detected upon transfection with ICAM1 Y474A+Y485 A (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: No rescue of tumor killing could be detected upon transfection with ICAM1 Y474A+Y485A.
source: The mutant ICAM1 P404E rescued tumor killing by CTLs to similar extent as full length ICAM1, whereas no rescue could be detected upon transfection with ICAM1 Y474A+Y485 A (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The ratio of mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 is important for the productive interaction between tumor cells and CTLs.
source: These data emphasize the importance of the ratio of mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 for the productive interaction between tumor cells and CTLs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: No significant change in killing could be detected upon expression of sICAM1 in ICAM1 KO cells.
source: No significant change in killing could be detected upon expression of sICAM1 in ICAM1 KO cells.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data.

claim: Overexpression of sICAM-1 in WT cells protected cells from CTL killing, possibly due to interference of sICAM-1 with mICAM-1/LFA-1 interaction.
source: Overexpression of sICAM-1 in WT cells had no impact on mICAM-1 expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) but protected cells from CTL killing, possibly due to interference of sICAM-1 with mICAM-1/LFA-1 interaction (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6B with a proposed mechanism.

claim: Addition of medium harvested from cells overexpressing sICAM-1 had no effect on tumor killing.
source: Addition of medium harvested from cells overexpressing sICAM-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, B) or medium with recombinant sICAM-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A, B) had no effect on tumor killing.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Addition of medium with recombinant sICAM-1 had no effect on tumor killing.
source: Addition of medium harvested from cells overexpressing sICAM-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, B) or medium with recombinant sICAM-1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A, B) had no effect on tumor killing.
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: Cells must produce sICAM-1 to be protected from CTL killing.
source: These results demonstrate that cells must produce sICAM-1 to be protected from CTL killing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Truncation of cytoplasmic tail of ICAM-1 (ICAM1-ΔC) did not alter rescue of tumor cell killing compared to full-length ICAM1.
source: Truncation of cytoplasmic tail of ICAM-1 (ICAM1-ΔC) did not alter rescue of tumor cell killing compared to full-length ICAM1 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: ICAM1-ΔTM-ΔC-GPI was not as efficient as full-length ICAM1 in rescuing tumor killing.
source: However, ICAM1-ΔTM-ΔC-GPI was not as efficient as full-length ICAM1 in rescuing tumor killing (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 play opposite roles in the interaction of CTL with tumor cells.
source: In summary, mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 play opposite roles in the interaction of CTL with tumor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: mICAM-1 promotes tumor killing by CTL.
source: mICAM-1 promotes tumor killing by CTL whereas sICAM-1 increases resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: sICAM-1 increases resistance to tumor killing by CTL.
source: mICAM-1 promotes tumor killing by CTL whereas sICAM-1 increases resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ICAM-1 is constitutively expressed and up-regulated by inflammatory activation such as stimulation by TNF-α or IFN-γ.
source: ICAM-1 is constitutively expressed and up-regulated by inflammatory activation such as stimulation by TNF-α or IFN-γ (Becker et al., 1991; Figenschau et al., 2018; Ramos et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both TNF-α and IFN-γ enhanced mICAM-1 expression in all cell lines tested.
source: Both TNF-α and IFN-γ enhanced mICAM-1 expression and induced release of sICAM-1 in all cell lines tested suggesting this mechanism in generalizable across different cancer types (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Both TNF-α and IFN-γ induced release of sICAM-1 in all cell lines tested.
source: Both TNF-α and IFN-γ enhanced mICAM-1 expression and induced release of sICAM-1 in all cell lines tested suggesting this mechanism in generalizable across different cancer types (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The release of sICAM-1 induced by the combination of TNF-α and IFN-γ was higher than that induced by the individual cytokines.
source: The release of sICAM-1 induced by the combination of both was higher than that induced by the individual cytokines (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The mechanism of ICAM-1 regulation by TNF-α and IFN-γ is generalizable across different cancer types.
source: Both TNF-α and IFN-γ enhanced mICAM-1 expression and induced release of sICAM-1 in all cell lines tested suggesting this mechanism in generalizable across different cancer types (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The soluble form of ICAM-1 is generated by alternative splicing of ICAM1 or proteolytic cleavage of mICAM-1 through human neutrophil elastase, cathepsin G, MMP-9, ADAM10 and ADAM17.
source: The soluble form of ICAM-1 is generated by alternative splicing of ICAM1 or proteolytic cleavage of mICAM-1 through human neutrophil elastase, cathepsin G, MMP-9, ADAM10 and ADAM17 (Fiore et al., 2002; Morsing et al., 2021; Robledo et al., 2003; Tsakadze et al., 2006; Wakatsuki et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: All normal healthy tissue types analyzed expressed ICAM1 at varying basal levels.
source: All normal healthy tissue types analyzed expressed ICAM1 at varying basal levels (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In 12 human cancers ICAM1 was significantly upregulated compared to normal tissue.
source: In 12 human cancers it was significantly upregulated compared to normal tissue.
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis.

claim: MMP9 expression was elevated in all tumor types compared to normal.
source: Moreover, MMP9 expression was elevated in all tumor types compared to normal (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: In some tumor types expression of ADAM10 and ADAM17 was increased compared to normal tissue.
source: In some tumor types expression of ADAM10 and ADAM17 was increased compared to normal tissue.
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis.

claim: Expression of ELANE and CTSG was lower compared to normal tissue.
source: Expression of ELANE and CTSG was lower compared to normal tissue.
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis.

claim: High expression of ICAM1 and high expression of MMP9 was related to shorter survival in glioblastoma multiforme patients.
source: We found high expression of ICAM1 and high expression of MMP9 was related to shorter survival in glioblastoma multiforme patients (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA survival analysis shown in Figure 7E.

claim: High expression of ICAM1 and high expression of ADAM10 or ADAM17 was associated with poor clinical outcome in pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients.
source: Moreover, high expression of ICAM1 and high expression of ADAM10 or ADAM17 was associated with poor clinical outcome in pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA survival analysis shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The expression of the combination of ICAM1 and protease have a worse impact on survival than each gene alone.
source: The expression of the combination of ICAM1 and protease have a worse impact on survival than each gene alone (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the TCGA survival analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of ICAM1 and ICAM-1 cleavage related metalloproteinases is elevated in various human cancers.
source: Collectively, expression of ICAM1 and ICAM-1 cleavage related metalloproteinases is elevated in various human cancers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCGA and GTEx data analysis.

claim: High co-expression of ICAM1 and MMP9, ADAM10, or ADAM17 is associated with poor clinical outcome.
source: Moreover, high co-expression of ICAM1 and MMP9, ADAM10, or ADAM17 is associated with poor clinical outcome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCGA survival analysis.

claim: CTL-mediated tumor cell killing is modulated by mICAM-1 level and release of sICAM-1.
source: Altogether, our data suggest that CTL-mediated tumor cell killing is modulated by mICAM-1 level and release of sICAM-1 (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ICAM-1 contributes to the formation of a productive immunological synapse leading to tumor killing.
source: While ICAM-1 contributes to the formation of a productive immunological synapse leading to tumor killing, its absence or release of sICAM-1 inhibits tumor cell killing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The absence of ICAM-1 or release of sICAM-1 inhibits tumor cell killing.
source: While ICAM-1 contributes to the formation of a productive immunological synapse leading to tumor killing, its absence or release of sICAM-1 inhibits tumor cell killing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The depletion of ILKAP induced increased tumor sensitivity to antigen-specific CTL killing in both HCT 116 and Panc-1 cell lines.
source: The depletion of ILKAP induced increased tumor sensitivity to antigen-specific CTL killing in both cell lines which correlated with remaining expression (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8A–C.

claim: The effect of ILKAP depletion on CTL-mediated tumor killing correlated with remaining expression.
source: The depletion of ILKAP induced increased tumor sensitivity to antigen-specific CTL killing in both cell lines which correlated with remaining expression (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8A–C.

claim: The effect of ILKAP depletion and basal expression in Panc-1 cells on CTL-mediated tumor killing was more moderate compared to HCT 116 cells.
source: The effect of ILKAP depletion and basal expression in Panc-1 cells on CTL-mediated tumor killing was more moderate compared to HCT 116 cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: No significant difference in cell death between ILKAP KO and control cells upon IFN-γ or TNFα stimulation could be detected.
source: No significant difference in cell death between ILKAP KO and control cells upon IFN-γ or TNFα stimulation could be detected (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Upregulation of HLA-A2, ICAM-1 and PD-L1 was similar between ILKAP KO and control cells upon INF-γ or TNF-α stimulation.
source: Upregulation of HLA-A2, ICAM-1 and PD-L1 was similar between ILKAP KO and control cells upon INF-γ or TNF-α stimulation (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: ILKAP KO cells showed an enhanced basal level of ICAM-1 compared to control cells.
source: Interestingly, ILKAP KO cells showed an enhanced basal level of ICAM-1 compared to control cells, whereas PD-L1 and HLA-A2 levels were similar (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: PD-L1 and HLA-A2 basal levels were similar between ILKAP KO and control cells.
source: Interestingly, ILKAP KO cells showed an enhanced basal level of ICAM-1 compared to control cells, whereas PD-L1 and HLA-A2 levels were similar (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: A non-significant decrease of mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 was observed following transient transfection of ILKAP but not catalytic dead ILKAP (H154D).
source: We observed a non-significant decrease of mICAM-1 and sICAM-1 following transient transfection of ILKAP but not catalytic dead ILKAP (H154D) (Figure 8H and I).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data shown in Figure 8H and I.

claim: ILKAP deletion enhances tumor killing independently of increasing sensitivity to IFNγ or TNF.
source: Taken together, these results show that ILKAP deletion enhances tumor killing independently of increasing sensitivity to IFNγ or TNF.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ILKAP KO led to concomitant increase in mICAM-1.
source: ILKAP KO led to concomitant increase in mICAM-1 but ILKAP overexpression had minor impact on surface ICAM-1 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ILKAP overexpression had minor impact on surface ICAM-1 expression.
source: ILKAP KO led to concomitant increase in mICAM-1 but ILKAP overexpression had minor impact on surface ICAM-1 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The characterization of the potential regulation of ICAM-1 by ILKAP would need further investigation.
source: The characterization of the potential regulation of ICAM-1 by ILKAP would need further investigation.
evidence: This is a statement about the need for future research.

claim: A complementary CRISPR screen was developed to identify tumor intrinsic genetic determinants that control tumor susceptibility to CTL-mediated killing.
source: We developed a complementary CRISPR screen to identify tumor intrinsic genetic determinants that control tumor susceptibility to CTL-mediated killing.
evidence: This describes the main approach of the study.

claim: The complementary CRISPR screen combined a CRISPRa screen with a CRISPR KO screen to study upregulation of genes that are not expressed endogenously at high levels.
source: In contrast to previous studies, we combined a CRISPRa screen with a CRISPR KO screen to study upregulation of genes that are not expressed endogenously at high levels.
evidence: This describes the novelty of the approach.

claim: Due to the external loading of tumor cells with the respective antigenic peptide, tumor intrinsic antigen processing and presentation pathways are not detectable allowing mapping of gene hits besides this tumor evasion strategy.
source: Due to the external loading of tumor cells with the respective antigenic peptide, tumor intrinsic antigen processing and presentation pathways are not detectable allowing us to map gene hits besides this tumor evasion strategy.
evidence: This is an explanation of a feature of the experimental design.

claim: The complementary CRISPR approach uncovered ILKAP as novel regulator of tumor sensitivity to CTL killing.
source: Our approach uncovered ILKAP as novel regulator of tumor sensitivity to CTL killing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the screen data.

claim: ILKAP was first identified in a yeast two-hybrid screen associated with Integrin-linked kinase 1 (ILK1) and shown to negatively regulate ILK1 activity thereby targeting ILK1 signaling components of Wnt pathway.
source: ILKAP was first identified in a yeast two-hybrid screen associated with Integrin-linked kinase 1 (ILK1) and shown to negatively regulate ILK1 activity thereby targeting ILK1 signaling components of Wnt pathway (Leung-Hagesteijn et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the context of cancer, ILKAP was described to regulate the susceptibility of ovarian tumor cells to cisplatin.
source: In the context of cancer, ILKAP was described to regulate the susceptibility of ovarian tumor cells to cisplatin, a platinum-based anti-cancer drug (Lorenzato et al., 2016), but never associated with antigen-specific tumor killing by CTLs.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ILKAP was never associated with antigen-specific tumor killing by CTLs prior to this study.
source: In the context of cancer, ILKAP was described to regulate the susceptibility of ovarian tumor cells to cisplatin, a platinum-based anti-cancer drug (Lorenzato et al., 2016), but never associated with antigen-specific tumor killing by CTLs.
evidence: This statement is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: ILK regulates ICAM-1 expression via NF-κB signaling.
source: It was previously shown that ILK regulates ICAM-1 expression via NF-κB signaling (Lee et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ILKAP regulates ICAM-1 basal levels through modulating ILK signaling.
source: Since we observed a trend towards decreased levels of ICAM-1 upon overexpression of ILKAP but not with the catalytic inactive mutant ILKAP (H154), we suggest that ILKAP regulates ICAM-1 basal levels through modulating ILK signaling.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data and previous literature.

claim: The minor impact of ILKAP overexpression compared to deletion could be explained by already high level of ILKAP phosphatase activity in untransfected cells that may not be dramatically increased upon overexpression.
source: The minor impact of overexpression compared to deletion could be explained by already high level of ILKAP phosphatase activity in untransfected cells that may not be dramatically increased upon overexpression.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data.

claim: Stimulation of ILKAP KO cells with IFN-γ and TNFα revealed that ILKAP-mediated tumor protection against CTL killing is independent from controlling INF-γ or TNFα sensitivity, changing PD-L1 levels and regulating antigen presentation.
source: Stimulation of ILKAP KO cells with IFN-γ and TNFα revealed that ILKAP-mediated tumor protection against CTL killing is independent from controlling INF-γ or TNFα sensitivity, changing PD-L1 levels and regulating antigen presentation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: ICAM-1 plays several roles in the immune system including cellular adhesion, inflammation, wound healing, T cell activation and leukocyte recruitment.
source: ICAM-1 plays several roles in the immune system including cellular adhesion, inflammation, wound healing, T cell activation and leukocyte recruitment (Bui et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Surface ICAM-1 binds to LFA-1 on T cells and contributes to the formation of an immunological synapse between target cells and CTL during killing.
source: Importantly, surface ICAM-1 binds to LFA-1 on T cells and contribute to the formation of an immunological synapse between target cells and CTL during killing (Anikeeva et al., 2005; Franciszkiewicz et al., 2013) as well as antigen presenting cell and T cell during priming (Hartman et al., 2009; Scholer et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Surface ICAM-1 binds to LFA-1 on T cells and contributes to the formation of an immunological synapse between antigen presenting cell and T cell during priming.
source: Importantly, surface ICAM-1 binds to LFA-1 on T cells and contribute to the formation of an immunological synapse between target cells and CTL during killing (Anikeeva et al., 2005; Franciszkiewicz et al., 2013) as well as antigen presenting cell and T cell during priming (Hartman et al., 2009; Scholer et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: From the tumor side, ICAM-1 appears to be important for the physical interaction with CTL with little signaling function in this context.
source: From the tumor side, ICAM-1 appears to be important for the physical interaction with CTL with little signaling function in this context (Basu et al., 2016; Petit et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Expression of ICAM1 missing the cytoplasmic domain rescued killing to the same extent as full-length ICAM-1.
